Stop Julia processes started for ctsem

Source: R/ctJuliaProcesses.R
ctJuliaKill.Rd

Stops the Julia processes ctJuliaProcesses lists. By default only those left by R sessions that have ended, which nothing can be using.

Usage

ctJuliaKill(
  which = c("orphaned", "session", "workers", "mine", "all"),
  pid = NULL,
  ask = interactive()
)

Arguments

which

Which to stop. "orphaned" (the default) stops processes whose R session has ended. "session" stops this R session's engine, which the next julia call replaces with a new one that has to compile again. "workers" stops this session's sampling workers, the background R sessions that sampling with processes = TRUE keeps for the next call, with their Julia processes. "mine" stops all three, and "all" every process listed, including the engines of other running R sessions, which then fail.

pid

Process ids to stop instead of choosing by which. Only processes ctJuliaProcesses() lists can be stopped this way.

ask

Whether to ask before stopping another R session's engine, as which = "all" or pid can.

Value

The rows of ctJuliaProcesses() that were stopped, invisibly.

See also

ctJuliaProcesses

Examples

# \donttest{
ctJuliaKill()             # engines left by R sessions that have ended
ctJuliaKill("session")    # this session's engine, e.g. stuck compiling
# }
